# evo-skillopt — llms-full.txt

Full LLM-navigable summary. Shaped so an agent that reads only this
file still has enough to understand what the service does, call it
safely, and locate the source for anything deeper.

Convention: [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org/).

## One-line description

A self-hostable HTTP worker that evolves a Markdown "skill" file for an
LLM agent against a held-out eval set — rollout → reflect → aggregate →
select → update → gate — without touching model weights.

## Why it exists

Every AI agent product ships a v1.0 system prompt and iterates via
ad-hoc edits. evo-skillopt makes that iteration disciplined: epochs,
batches, validation gates, git-tracked audit trails. The compounding
advantage is the eval sets and evolved skill artifacts a team builds up
in their own repo over time, not the code (which is MIT).

## Not what it is

- Not a new training algorithm — SkillOpt itself ([arXiv:2605.23904])
  is the upstream project. This repo productizes it as a service.
- Not a new LLM. Works with any frozen model (OpenAI, Anthropic,
  Google, Azure OpenAI, Ollama, vLLM).
- Not a prompt-engineering IDE.
- Not an eval framework alone — evals are the gate, not the point.

## HTTP API (callable from any language)

### `GET /health` — liveness

Unauthenticated. Returns `{"service": "skillopt-worker", "status": "ok"}`.

### `POST /train` — one training pass

Bearer auth when `WORKER_TOKEN` is set. Payload:

```json
{
  "bot_id":               "author/name",
  "skill_version":        "0.1.0",
  "skill_path":           "/data/.../skills/main.md",
  "eval_split_dir":       "/data/.../eval",
  "config":               "configs/searchqa/default.yaml",
  "num_epochs":           1,
  "gate_min_improvement": 0.05,
  "rrss":                 { "...optional overlay": "..." }
}
```

Response:

```json
{
  "ok":                true,
  "gate_passed":       true,
  "gate_score_delta":  0.073,
  "next_version":      "0.1.1",
  "output_dir":        "outputs/evo/...",
  "duration_s":        412,
  "job_id":            "<uuid>",
  "rrss":              { "composite": 0.84, "robustify": 0.78, ... }
}
```

**Optional RRSS overlay** — scores the candidate on four resilience
axes (Robustify / Reliabilify / Solidify / Stabilize), accepts only
when every configured axis clears its floor AND the composite improves
by `min_improvement`. Set `rrss.auto_from_history: true` to derive
axis inputs from the run's `history.json` + rollouts.

### `POST /train/cascade` — gate a skill pipeline

Pure aggregation (no training). Payload:

```json
{
  "bot_id": "author/name",
  "stages": [
    { "name": "filter",   "score": 0.94 },
    { "name": "classify", "score": 0.88 },
    { "name": "draft",    "score": 0.91, "weight": 2.0 }
  ],
  "aggregation":         "mean | min | product | weighted_mean",
  "aggregate_threshold": 0.85,
  "stage_floor":         0.60
}
```

Passes iff every stage clears `stage_floor` AND the aggregate meets
`aggregate_threshold`. A fluent draft cannot mask a broken filter
upstream.

### `POST /fitness/arm` — compute lifecycle-weighted fitness

Pure aggregation. Payload:

```json
{
  "bot_id": "author/name",
  "signals": [
    { "bucket": "acquire",  "delta": 1.0, "kind": "trial_started" },
    { "bucket": "retain",   "delta": 0.5, "kind": "csat_5" },
    { "bucket": "monetize", "delta": 2.0, "kind": "plan_upgrade" }
  ],
  "weights": { "acquire": 0.3, "retain": 0.5, "monetize": 0.2 }
}
```

Rebalance weights over the lifecycle: launch ≈ 0.60/0.30/0.10, growth
≈ 0.30/0.50/0.20, mature ≈ 0.10/0.40/0.50. Weights are renormalized;
empty signals return 0 fitness without erroring.

## Repo map

- `README.md` — human overview
- `AGENTS.md` — AI-agent orientation
- `EvoSkillOpt_Blueprint.md` — vision, roadmap, KPIs
- `INSTALL.md`, `USE_CASES.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SECURITY.md`
- `worker/` — HTTP service + RRSS gate + cascade + ARM
- `scripts/` — training / eval CLIs
- `configs/` — per-benchmark YAML
- `examples/` — three runnable bot examples
- `skillopt/` — **vendored** upstream SkillOpt (MIT, do not edit)
- `tests/` — pytest suite covering the worker extensions
- `docs/` — mkdocs source

## How a safe agent should use the API

1. Read [`AGENTS.md`](./AGENTS.md) once for repo conventions.
2. Call `GET /health` before anything else.
3. Prefer the pure endpoints (`/train/cascade`, `/fitness/arm`) when
   training is not strictly required — they return in milliseconds.
4. On `/train`, respect `gate_passed`: a `false` means the previous
   skill version stays active. Do not auto-retry on a rejection.
5. Never commit secrets. Provider API keys live in env only
   (see `.env.example`).

[arXiv:2605.23904]: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23904
